name: Foam Roller IT Band
summary: A self-myofascial release technique that uses bodyweight against a foam roller to target the lateral thigh and tensor fasciae latae.

setup: Place a foam roller on the floor and lie on your side with the roller positioned under your outer hip, just below the hip joint.
Support your upper body on your forearm and place your top foot flat on the floor in front of or behind your bottom leg to help regulate the pressure.
steps: Slowly roll down your outer thigh from just below the hip bone toward the top of the knee.
Pause and hold on any particularly tender or tight areas for several seconds to allow the tissue to relax.
Roll back upward toward the hip in a smooth, controlled motion.
Complete the desired duration or number of passes, then switch to the other leg.
instructions.breathing: Maintain slow, deep, diaphragmatic breathing throughout, avoiding holding your breath when rolling over tender spots.
cues: Support your weight with your arms and top leg

common_faults.fault: Rolling directly over the knee joint or hip bone
common_faults.correction: Stop rolling just above the outer knee joint and remain below the greater trochanter of the hip.

common_faults.fault: Rolling too quickly across the tissue
common_faults.correction: Move slowly at a rate of one to two inches per second, pausing over trigger points.

common_faults.fault: Tensing the body and holding your breath due to discomfort
common_faults.correction: Offload more weight through your support arm and foot to reduce intensity to a tolerable level.

precautions: Avoid rolling directly onto bone or joint structures.
Discontinue if you experience sharp, radiating, or nerve pain.
